inputs.share_count_basis: Basic shares in issue at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin), post the 5-for-1 split of 2025-10-01. Held FLAT. The Y600bn convertible bonds issued March 2026 are carried as DEBT at face inside net_debt (they sit in 'Bonds, borrowings and lease liabilities'); the implied ~690m potential shares (Q1 FY2027 diluted EPS 12.73 vs basic 14.40 => ~5,915m diluted; conversion price ~Y870) are out of the money at the current price, so the debt treatment is the more conservative and self-consistent one. If-converted memo: equity +Y600bn, shares +~690m. Performance-linked stock compensation adds 0.18m shares (immaterial).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual tanshin, statement of changes in equity: share-based payment transactions Y318m (performance-linked stock compensation). Effectively an SBC-zero filer; no equity-award cash taxes disclosed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity ~9.5% = 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.3 x 6.0% JPY ERP (integrated steel, levered). After-tax cost of debt ~2.5% (blended JPY subordinated/JBIC/CB funding at 1-3% and USD U.S. Steel notes at ~6%, BBB/negative). Weighted at a 65/35 target equity/debt structure (management's adjusted D/E target of ~0.7x after hybrid equity credit, deleveraging via Y100bn+ asset sales and the Y600bn CB) gives ~7.0%. Market-value weights today (60% debt) would give ~5.3%; the house keiretsu reference of ~9% applies to net-cash suppliers where WACC = CoE. 7.0% charges leverage/cyclicality once in the rate; scenarios share the same WACC so risk is not charged again per scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities are not disclosed separately in the tanshin; they sit inside 'Bonds, borrowings and lease liabilities' (Y5,515.7bn at 2026-06-30) and therefore inside net_debt. No lease principal is deducted from the flows; EBITDA is the company's post-IFRS-16 figure (Business Profit + D&A). Right-of-use asset renewal is not separately charged -- lease liabilities are small against Y5.5tn of total borrowings.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests deducted once in the equity bridge at book (Y485,183m at 2026-06-30). NCI took 8-10% of group profit in normal years (FY2024 Y38.5bn, FY2025 Y32.7bn, FY2026 Y27.6bn).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (JPY WACC, leases as debt, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for associates and investment securities, SBC-zero). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; first valuation of this ticker, no memory entry. EBITDA MARGIN DEFINITION: company EBITDA (Business Profit + D&A, post-IFRS-16) EXCLUDING share of profit of equity-method investments (Y85.4bn FY2026, ~Y80bn implied by Q1 FY2027 run-rate; Y126.9bn FY2025) -- that stream is stripped and its source asset (investments accounted for using the equity method, Y1,493.1bn at 2026-06-30, incl. AM/NS India) is added in the equity bridge at book. Finance income (Y31.1bn, interest on cash/loans) is stripped as interest_income and the non-current 'other financial assets' (Y545.0bn, mainly FVOCI strategic shareholdings -- management plans Y100bn+ of sales in FY2027) are added in the bridge. Dividend income (~Y15bn, inside Business Profit) is left in the flows against those securities: a tolerance of <Y3/share, noted. FY0 = FY2026 = year ended 2026-03-31 (company 'fiscal 2025'); Y1 = year ending 2027-03-31 (company 'fiscal 2026', guided 2026-08-04: revenue Y11,200bn, Business Profit Y630bn, EBITDA Y1,330bn, capex ~Y1,430bn accrual basis, D&A ~Y700bn). MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: IFRS-basis (FY2018-FY2026) EBITDA margin incl. associates averaged 11.7% (12.9% ex the FY2020 impairment year; 2.2% trough FY2020, 18.6% peak FY2022); Business Profit margin averaged 6.2%. Base mature ex-associates EBITDA margin 12.0% (~13% incl. associates, Business Profit margin ~6.7%) sits a little above the historic mean to credit the tariff-protected U.S. mix and partial synergy delivery, well short of the 2030 plan's Y1tn underlying BP (~8% margin). FY2026's negative FCF (-Y146bn reported, -Y178bn owner) and the FY2027 capex bulge (Y1,430bn, ~12.8% of revenue accrual / ~11.5% cash) are modelled explicitly as a 3-year cash drain under the National Security Agreement ($10.8bn U.S. Steel investment by 2028) and then normalised to 6.5% of revenue (~1.0x D&A; FY2019-FY2026 cash capex averaged 7.25% of revenue). Net debt, shares, NCI and bridge assets are all from the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; the Y341bn debt increase in the June quarter is seasonal working capital plus capex. The subordinated term loan (Y500bn) and subordinated bonds are carried as full debt -- rating-agency equity credit is not an owner's equity. Buybacks: none; the flat count is a modelling convention (SBC-zero) rather than a funded one. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, so band_position is degenerate (null).

historical_growth.basis: IFRS years only (FY2018 onward); J-GAAP FY2013-FY2017 excluded from any CAGR. FY2026 = year ended 2026-03-31. Share-based figures on today's post-split basis.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: post-consolidation mid-cycle nominal JPY growth (flat Japan volumes, India/U.S. growth, ~2% inflation); historical revenue and equity CAGRs are inflated by the June 2025 U.S. Steel consolidation (revenue +15.7% in FY2026 on consolidation alone) and the Y297bn FY2025 convertible conversion, and are not a forward proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.9% vs revenue 15.8% agree, but both are acquisition- and conversion-driven. EPS CAGRs are null: diluted EPS fell from Y134.38 (FY2023) to Y3.28 (FY2026) on Y271bn of reorganisation losses, and the FY2021 base is negative. Owner-FCF CAGRs null: FY2026 owner FCF is -Y178bn (acquisition-year capex), FY2021 base negative.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF history (reported FCF less finance income, Y bn): FY2018 68, FY2019 8, FY2020 26, FY2021 -62, FY2022 147, FY2023 183, FY2024 522, FY2025 360, FY2026 -178. Nine-year mean Y120bn = 1.6% of revenue; FY2022-FY2025 (upcycle) mean Y303bn = 3.7%. Base case mature owner-FCF margin ~3.6% therefore embeds upcycle-average cash conversion, not the full-cycle mean -- the bear case carries the full-cycle figure.

base.narrative: Y1 = FY2027 guidance (revenue Y11.2tn = +11.3% on a full year of U.S. Steel; ex-associates EBITDA ~Y1,235bn = 11.0%; D&A Y700bn; cash capex ~Y1,290bn against Y1,430bn accrual). Growth then 3% fading to 2% nominal JPY. EBITDA margin drifts up 1pp over five years as U.S. Steel synergies ($0.3bn 2026, blast-furnace restarts) and domestic consolidation (Sanyo Special Steel 2027, Krosaki Harima) partly offset China-export spread pressure, maturing at 12.0% ex-associates -- around the IFRS-era mid-cycle. Capex runs 11.5%/10.5%/9.5% of revenue through FY2029 (NSA $10.8bn commitment) then normalises to 6.5% (~1.0x D&A). Working capital consumes 8% of incremental revenue (receivables + inventory > payables). Cash tax 30% on EBIT (Japan ~30.6%, U.S. ~25%). Terminal: 1.5% growth, cap 15x FCF (~4x mature EBITDA, below the stock's own 5-7x EV/EBITDA range).

bull.narrative: The 2030 plan is delivered: U.S. Steel's $3bn structural EBITDA improvement lands by 2030 behind Section 232 pricing, AM/NS India and Rajayapeta volumes grow with Indian demand (~7-8%/yr), domestic consolidation takes cost out, and a GX-steel premium starts to form. Ex-associates EBITDA margin reaches 13.5% (~14.5% incl. associates, Business Profit ~8% = the Y1tn underlying BP target on ~Y12.5tn revenue). Capex normalises faster (6.0% of revenue) once the NSA programme completes in 2028; U.S. NOLs and bonus depreciation hold cash tax at 28%.

bear.narrative: FY2027 misses guidance (Middle East raw-material/fuel costs and lost Middle East exports, which management explicitly excluded from the forecast; a weaker USD/JPY than the Y160 assumed), then two flat years as OECD-projected excess capacity (745mt by 2028) and record Chinese exports keep Asian spreads at trough and U.S. prices mean-revert. Domestic underlying BP stays at or below the Y380bn just guided; U.S. Steel synergies disappoint. Ex-associates EBITDA margin settles at 10.5% (~11.5% incl. associates), i.e. the full-cycle FY2018-FY2026 IFRS mean including the FY2020 trough, rather than the upcycle. The NSA and golden share prevent capex from being cut: 11.5%/11%/10% of revenue through FY2029, normalising only to 7.0%. Interest-bearing debt of Y5.5tn then dominates the bridge: this path is an equity-is-an-option outcome and the DCF equity value sits at or below zero -- the finding is that Nippon Steel's equity does not survive a full-cycle-average margin with the committed capex, absent asset sales or equity issuance.

scenario_narratives.base: Full-year U.S. Steel consolidation and FY2027 guidance as the anchor, 3% fading to 2% nominal growth, ex-associates EBITDA margin maturing at 12.0% (just above the IFRS-era mid-cycle, partial synergy credit), three years of NSA-driven capex burn then 6.5% of revenue, 7.0% JPY WACC, 15x FCF terminal cap. Equity is a thin slice on Y5.0tn of net debt: every 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is roughly Y130-150/share.
scenario_narratives.bull: 2030 plan delivered -- Y1tn underlying Business Profit, U.S. Steel $3bn structural EBITDA uplift, India growth, GX-steel premium; capex normalises to 6% by FY2031; 28% cash tax. The leverage that crushes the bear case works in reverse here.
scenario_narratives.bear: Guidance miss on Middle East costs and USD/JPY, two flat years as Chinese overcapacity holds spreads at trough, margin settles at the full-cycle mean (10.5% ex-associates), NSA-locked capex cannot be cut. Enterprise value does not cover net debt plus NCI even with the Y2.0tn of associates and securities added back; equity value floors at zero. A further S&P downgrade from BBB/negative is the signpost.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: net debt Y5.0tn (D/E 0.94x reported) on a BBB/negative rating, capex locked by the National Security Agreement through 2028, FY2026 net profit Y17bn against a Y146bn dividend, and an unquantified Middle East cost that management excluded from guidance -- the downside is a solvency-shaped outcome, not just margin compression. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (U.S. Steel synergies at the $3bn scale, Asian spreads recovering against rising Chinese exports, and capex normalising on the NSA schedule). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nippon Steel is valued as a levered, cyclical, capital-intensive operating company on unlevered owner FCF with the balance sheet handled in the bridge: Y5.5tn of bonds, borrowings, leases, hybrids and the Y600bn CB as debt; Y1.49tn of equity-method investments and Y0.55tn of securities added at book under the matching-asset rule; NCI deducted at book. Mid-cycle normalisation is the whole argument -- FY2026 is an acquisition-year distortion (negative FCF, Y863bn capex, Y271bn reorganisation losses) and FY2022-FY2023 were a spread peak. The base case credits a margin a little above the IFRS-era mean and a capex bulge that runs three more years before normalising. Because equity is ~40% of enterprise value, the per-share value is extremely sensitive to the mature margin and to the capex normalisation level; the house 15x FCF terminal cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 7%/1.5% would be ~18.5x) and keeps the model from paying for a re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mature EBITDA margin: each 1pp ex-associates is ~Y130-150/share; the base 12.0% is above the FY2018-FY2026 mean (10.7% ex-associates) and relies on U.S. tariff pricing and synergy delivery persisting

Capex normalisation: the model assumes cash capex falls from ~11.5% to 6.5% of revenue by FY2031; the NSA $10.8bn commitment, Nagoya hot-strip mill, Rajayapeta Phase 1 and EAF/decarbonisation spend could keep it at 8%+ (each 1pp of steady-state capex is ~Y300/share)

Equity-method investments and securities taken at book Y2.04tn (~Y390/share); AM/NS India could be worth more, but the strategic shareholdings being sold could realise less than carrying value and the stripped associate income is being capitalised at ~15x

Convertible bond treatment: carried as Y600bn debt with basic shares; if the stock rallies through ~Y870, conversion adds ~690m shares (13%) and removes Y600bn of debt -- roughly neutral to IV at that price, dilutive above it
Cyclical timing: a down-cycle in FY2027-FY2029 while capex is locked would push the bear path, where DCF equity is zero, into the base
USD/JPY: ~25-30% of EBITDA and a large share of debt are now USD; the FY2027 guidance assumes Y160/$
